subject: Embeddings model fit validation & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings validation discussion / next steps

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning — that was helpful. As discussed, the core ask from our side is to validate an embeddings model for semantic search over our clinical knowledge base (PDFs, notes, and a small set of internal FAQs). We want to be confident on:

- retrieval quality (precision@10, MRR)
- robustness to drift (we have quarterly content updates)
- inference cost per query (we run ~150k queries/month)

To move forward, could you share a recommended evaluation plan and the models you think we should test? We can provide a 5k-document sample export (anonymized) and a set of 50 canonical queries + 200 relevance judgments.

Also please include any sample prompt sets or feature recommendations (vector dimensionality, normalization, distance metric) — we want to avoid surprises on quality regressions when we later scale.

We’re aiming to start a 6-week pilot in Aug if the evaluation looks good.

Cheers,
Samir
Director of Search & Knowledge Management
Acme Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings validation discussion / next steps

Samir — thank you for the clear summary and the sample timeline. Quick recap + recommended plan below.

Recap from call:
- Goal: semantic search on clinical KB with strong P@10 and MRR, low drift risk, predictable cost for ~150k q/mo
- Data: PDFs, notes, FAQs (you’ll provide 5k anonymized docs + 50 queries + 200 judgments)
- Timeline: evaluation in 1-2 weeks after we receive data; pilot kickoff in Aug (6 weeks)

Recommended evaluation plan (what we’ll run):
1) Candidate models: 
   - redwood-embed-v2-large (1536d) — strong balance of quality/cost for domain text
   - text-embed-6-large (1536d) — baseline open model for comparison
   - text-embed-6-small (512d) — low-cost option for throughput testing
2) Metrics: P@1/5/10, MRR, Recall@k (k=50), and cosine similarity distributions. We’ll also compute embedding drift via centroid movement & average pairwise distances over time.
3) Dimensionality / distance: prefer 1536 dims for best semantic fidelity; we’ll test 512d to measure cost/quality tradeoffs. Use cosine similarity for retrieval; we can include dot-product as a quick sanity check.
4) Evaluation artifacts: prompt/embedding preproc set (tokenization, stopword handling), seed query set, and the judge file (200 labels). We’ll output result dashboards + qualitative failure cases.
5) Regression guardrails: we’ll run a baseline vs your current search and flag any >5% drop in MRR or >7% drop in P@10 as a regression.

Attachments I’m sending: redwood-proposal-acme-v1.pdf (proposal/estimate), acme_semantic_search_benchmarks.pdf (example benchmark schema), acme_prompt-set-v1.csv (example prompt/queries).

Next steps / asks for Acme:
- Share anonymized 5k docs + CSV of 50 queries + 200 judgments (S3 link or Drive) by Fri 24 Jul
- Confirm which models you want us to prioritize (we recommend starting with redwood-embed-v2-large + text-embed-6-large)
- Confirm pilot budget window (approx estimate included in the attached proposal)

Rishi and Marissa — looping you in for technical validation and to scope compute/throughput for the pilot. Rishi, can you confirm the expected cost per 1k queries for the three model configs (1536 large, 1536 baseline, 512 small)?

Samir — happy to set a 30-min sync next week to walk through the evaluation dashboard once we ingest data.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings validation discussion / next steps

Thanks — quick technical notes from our side (cc’ing Samir so Acme sees the details):

- Preprocessing: we recommend normalizing text (lowercase, unicode normalize), preserve medical abbreviations using a whitelist, and strip boilerplate headers from PDFs. That reduces noisy tokens and improves embedding consistency.
- Sampling: for the initial eval, 5k docs + 50 queries is fine. If you can also include a small longitudinal slice (100 docs per quarter for last 12 months) we’ll compute drift metrics.
- Embedding size: 1536d gives better semantic separation on clinical terms; we’ll include a 512d run to quantify cost tradeoffs. Expect ~6-9% drop in MRR moving to 512d on medical text in our prior pilots.
- Similarity / retrieval tuning: start with cosine + k=10, and run a small sweep on normalization (L2 vs no-norm) to check P@10 sensitivity.
- Quality checks: we’ll surface top 100 failure cases for human review (confusing synonyms, abbreviations, date-sensitive docs).

I’ll prepare a short eval plan doc (one-pager) and a dashboard link once Marcus uploads the dataset. Rishi — I’ll need a quick cost estimate for the three configs to add to the proposal.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Retrieval | Redwood Inference
